Cassian said I had to.|K-2SO to Jyn Erso|}} '''K-2SO''' was a modified [[KX-series security droid]] who served in the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]]. Originally created for the [[Imperial Army]], the [[droid]] was deployed in [[2 BBY]] as part of the [[Galactic Empire]]'s efforts to quell protests on the [[planet]] [[Ghorman]]. After the [[Ghorman Massacre]] and encountering the [[Axis network]] operative [[Cassian Jeron Andor]], K-2SO was incapacitated by [[Samm]], a member of the [[Ghorman Front]], and salvaged by Andor. Upon their return to the [[Great Temple]] rebel base on [[Yavin 4]], K-2SO was repaired and reprogrammed to serve the Rebel Alliance. The droid became a friend and companion to Andor on various missions for the Alliance. In [[1 BBY]], K-2SO participated in the [[Raid on the Axis safehouse|rescue]] of the [[Axis network]] rebel [[Kleya Marki]], along with the rebel [[Ruescott Melshi]]. Marki would pass along intelligence about a secret Imperial weapon that the Alliance would soon learn was the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]] [[battle station]], a [[moon]]-sized [[superweapon]]. K-2SO was then sent to [[Wobani]] to help [[Liberation of Erso|rescue]] the Imperial [[prisoner]] [[Jyn Erso]], who the rebels believed could help them locate the Imperial [[scientist]] associated with the weapon, namely [[Galen Walton Erso|Galen Erso]], Jyn's father. After K-2SO assisted in the rescue, he joined Andor and Jyn in visiting the moon [[Jedha]], where they would attempt to use Jyn as a mediator to speak with the extremist rebel [[Saw Gerrera]], as he had taken the Imperial pilot [[Bodhi Rook]] prisoner after they had defected at the behest of Galen. Although K-2SO initially was ordered to stay with the [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|ship]], he assisted his companions during a [[Battle on Jedha|fight]] between Gerrera's [[Partisans]] and local Imperial forces. After extracting Rook and also being joined by the Jedha citizens [[Chirrut Îmwe]] and [[Baze Malbus]], K-2SO rescued Andor, Jyn, and their new companions as the Death Star [[Destruction of Jedha City|destroyed]] [[Jedha City]] with its [[superlaser]]. En route to the planet [[Eadu]] to locate Galen, K-2SO helped pilot the ship but nonetheless crash-landed outside the [[Eadu Flight Station]]. While Andor and Rook approached the Imperial installation, K-2SO discovered that a [[Blue Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|squadron]] of Alliance [[starfighter]]s was approaching. As a battle commenced, K-2SO and the others extracted themselves with a stolen [[SW-0608|Imperial shuttle]]. After the incident on Eadu, [[Alliance High Command]] refused to act on the intelligence that Jyn had received on Jedha: her father had set a trap in the Death Star, which the rebels needed the [[Death Star plans]] to exploit. However, Andor had other ideas. He assembled a [[Rogue One|team]] of rebels, which included K-2SO to steal the plans from the Empire's [[Citadel Tower]] on the planet [[Scarif]]. K-2 would infiltrate the base with Andor and Jyn as their allies engaged the Imperial forces in [[Battle of Scarif|battle]], with the goal of finding the plans. At the [[Scarif vault]], K-2SO sacrificed himself so that Andor and Jyn could steal the plans and transmit them to the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance fleet]]. ==Biography== ===Imperial droid=== ====The enforcer==== {{Quote|I have carried out many Imperial directives prior to my reprogramming. Killing, maiming, kidnapping, arson, telemarketing. My orders were usually intended to do harm to the Rebel cause, is that what you mean?|K-2SO, during a mandatory psychological check-in|''[[REBELIÓN: An Andor Zine]]''}} [[File:K-2SOblueprints.jpg|thumb|right|240px|Technical drawing of a KX-series security droid]] K-2SO was a [[KX-series security droid]] built in [[12 BBY]] on the [[planet]] [[Vulpter]]. K-2SO would serve the [[Galactic Empire]]. At some point, he took part in an Imperial parade on the planet [[Coruscant]] among two hundred total KX-series [[droid]]s. The droid noticed the [[Galactic Emperor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine's]] presence at the parade as well.{{Andor|Who Else Knows?}} During his Imperial service, K-2SO conducted a series of directives aimed at quelling resistance to the Empire, ranging from [[telemarketing]] to [[Death|killing]]. In [[2 BBY]], as the Empire began to arrange the conditions for a protest on the planet [[Ghorman]], [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[Major]] [[Lio Partagaz]] assigned [[Captain]] [[Kaido]] and a [[Ghorman crisis team|crisis team]] to Ghorman. K-2SO was one of several KX units sent to Ghorman. The droids were kept inside the [[Imperial office complex]] in the main [[Palmo Plaza|plaza]] of the planet's capital [[city]], [[Palmo]], as the Imperial forces withdrew to the complex, an action that invited a force of hundreds of [[Ghorman (people)|Ghormans]] to peacefully yet determinedly assemble in the plaza to resist the Empire's oppressive reign. When [[Imperial Bureau of Standards]] employee [[Syril Karn]] entered the building and stumbled upon the droids, who were waiting to be deployed, Karn became concerned.{{Andor|Who Are You?}} ====A turning point==== {{Quote|Hello. If I've offended you, I apologize. If not, I'd appreciate you pointing that elsewhere.|K-2SO, to Cassian Jeron Andor, after being reactivated following his reprogramming|{{Andor|Welcome to the Rebellion}}}} When a [[Bloy's riot squad|team]] of [[Imperial security trooper]]s advanced into the crowd, an Imperial [[sniper]] fired on one of their own men, causing the squad, thinking the Ghormans had attacked them, into turning their weapons on the protestors. As what would become the [[Ghorman Massacre]] broke out, the droids were let loose. K-2SO personally [[Death|killed]] several individuals, and as the protestors began to flee, he eventually made his way out of the plaza and onto the surrounding streets. There, he began to pursue [[Axis network]] operatives [[Wilmon Paak]] and [[Cassian Jeron Andor]]. Andor fired several shots at the [[security droid]] in an attempt to stop him, but was fruitless in his efforts. Before K-2SO could reach Andor, however, [[Samm]]—a member of the insurgent group [[Ghorman Front]]—arrived on a [[Unidentified troop transport|repulsorcraft]], ramming into K-2SO and incapacitating him. [[File:WhoAreYou-AltThumbnail.png|thumb|300px|left|Andor made the decision to salvage K-2SO before leaving Ghorman.]] Before Andor, Paak, and Samm fled, Andor—who had been taught by his adoptive father, the salvager [[Clem Andor]], to never overlook the possibilities of seemingly useless, abandoned equipment{{Andor|Rix Road (episode)}}—requested that they help him salvage K-2SO's remains, which were quickly placed within the repulsorcraft before Andor used it to escape the city. After returning to [[Yavin 4]] following both the Ghorman Massacre and the [[Escape from the Senate|extraction]] of [[Chandrilan]] [[senator]] [[Mon Mothma]] from the [[Imperial Senate]] on the planet [[Coruscant]], Andor turned K-2SO's remains over to [[Alliance to Restore the Republic]] [[technician]]s so the [[droid]] could be rebuilt and reprogrammed. The following morning, the technicians informed Andor that they were about to attempt to reactivate K-2SO. Andor and multiple other rebels aimed their [[blaster]]s at K-2SO as he was reactivated. After spasming for a moment, K-2SO focused on Andor, apologized for offending him, and requested he stop aiming at him. ===Serving the Rebellion=== ====Alliance missions==== {{Quote|I am a reprogrammed Imperial droid.|K-2SO|}} [[File:AndorK2Wookiees-SWA-WookieeSitting.png|thumb|245px|right|K-2SO and Andor with Wookiee children.]] K-2SO and Andor were sent to the [[F'tzner system]] to undertake a [[Raid on an Imperial freighter|raid]] on an Imperial [[freighter]]. Andor used gas to trick the Empire into thinking that [[smuggler]]s stole the cargo, as smugglers were known to use gas to raid [[transport]]s. When they got to the cargo room, they found three [[Wookiee]]s named [[D'Koetaa]], [[D'Lylaa]], and [[Wyhyatt]], and took them instead of the cargo. Andor then took them to the monastery [[moon]] of [[Charissia]] in the [[Bartahn sector]]. There, he left K-2SO to look after the three Wookiees while Andor undertook a [[Unidentified Rebel raid|raid]].{{IDWAdventuresCite-2017|issue=3|story=Tales from Wild Space: Adventures in Wookiee-Sitting}} [[File:Rebels_infiltrate_Mustafar.png|thumb|left|250px|K-2SO on Mustafar.]] At some point K-2SO and [[Athex]] were sent to an [[Imperial base (Mustafar)|Imperial base]] near [[Fortress Vader]] on [[Mustafar]]. There, they assisted a team of rebels posing as stormtroopers in recovering for the Rebel Alliance. After the rebels stole the [[Proto-saber]], K-2SO picked up the rebels before [[Anakin Skywalker|Darth Vader]] could stop them from making their escape.''[[Star Wars: Secrets of the Empire]]'' At some point while stationed at the [[Great Temple|rebel base]] on Yavin 4, K-2SO had a run-in with [[R2-D2]] and [[C-3PO]], droids belonging to [[Raymus Antilles|the pilot]] of Senator [[Bail Prestor Organa|Bail Organa]].''[[Star Wars: The Rebel Files]]'' ====Coruscant-bound==== {{Quote|Are you with us?''"
"''No.|TAC 2C and K-2SO|}} In [[1 BBY]],{{AndorDate|211}} K-2SO was playing a game with Andor and [[Ruescott Melshi]] in Andor's abode. Melshi had just outsmarted K-2SO in the game, making the droid nervous—though K-2SO attempted to deny it. Immediately afterward, Paak arrived and revealed to the group that he had just received a coded transmission from [[Axis network]] liason [[Kleya Marki]]. After confirming the legitimacy of the signal and concluding that the leader of the Axis network, [[Luthen Rael]], was in danger, Andor, Melshi, and K-2SO departed to [[Raid on the Axis safehouse|rescue]] Rael and Marki—though K-2SO expressed reservations regarding the unauthorized nature of their mission. Upon arriving to the apartment complex housing the [[Axis network safehouse]] on Coruscant, Andor ordered K-2SO to remain in their [[UT-60D U-wing starfighter/support craft|U-wing]]. However, as Andor and Melshi worked to extract Marki—who confirmed that Rael had already [[Infiltration of Lina Soh Hospital|died]]—a group of [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[ISB tactical agent|tactical agents]] arrived, catching K-2SO's attention. In order to aid his allies, the security droid exited the U-wing and began to make his own way to the safehouse, dispatching multiple tactical agents and the pilot of their shuttle on his way there. Entering the apartment complex, K-2SO traveled through its halls and continued to take out multiple ISB agents, including their leader, [[Supervisor]] [[Avril Heert]], whom he utilized as a human shield. Upon reaching the safehouse, K-2SO and the group—a now-stunned Marki in tow—retreated to the U-wing and departed from Coruscant.{{Andor|Jedha, Kyber, Erso}} ====The Death Star==== {{Quote|There's a rumor we have a flight plan.''"
"''The Ring of Kafrene.''"
"''Tivik?''"
"''We'll take the quick way.''"
"''It's so much easier when I know what we're doing.|K-2SO and Cassian Andor|}} Upon their return to Yavin 4, Andor's commanding officer, [[General]] [[Davits Draven]], ordered K-2SO to power himself down as punishment for the group's excursion. The next day, however, K-2SO was put back into service when Andor received orders to investigate a claim made by [[Partisans|Partisan]] [[spy]] [[Tivik]] regarding a [[superweapon]] being constructed by Imperial architect [[Galen Walton Erso|Galen Erso]]—the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]]. As such, the duo departed to the [[Ring of Kafrene]] to correspond with Tivik. After Tivik relayed the intel to Andor—which had earlier been corroborated by Marki—he was killed, and the duo left the Ring of Kafrene. Afterwards, Andor{{InsiderCite|212|From the Shadows: The Dangerous Life of a Rebel Agent}} and K-2SO accompanied [[Extraction Team Bravo]], which helped Galen's daughter, [[Jyn Erso]], [[Liberation of Erso|escape]] from the [[Imperial Detention Center & Labor Camp LEG-817|Wobani Labor Camp]]. As Erso ran outside to escape, K-2SO seized Erso, threw her to the ground, and told her not to resist as she was being rescued. Bravo Team's U-wing transport, ''[[Bravo One]]'', encountered a minor technical setback and was unable to jump to [[hyperspace]]. The team took refuge in an [[asteroid field]] in [[Wobani system|Wobani's star system]], and K-2SO sent a priority transmission to all available Rebel [[Starship|vessels]]. An [[T-65B X-wing starfighter|X-wing starfighter]] [[squadron]] called [[Red Flight (Rebel Alliance)|Red Flight]] answered their call and saved them from incoming [[Imperial Navy|Imperial forces]]. Later, K-2SO accompanied Andor and Jyn on a mission to rescue Galen so that they could gather information about the [[Death Star]]. In secret, Cassian had received orders to kill Galen in order to prevent the weapon from being built. The Alliance had learned about the Death Star from the Imperial defector [[Bodhi Rook]], who had been taken by men working for [[Saw Gerrera]]. K-2SO was uncomfortable that Jyn had been given a blaster since she disliked him. ====Search for Galen Erso==== {{Quote|Did you know that wasn't me?''"
"''Of course.|K-2SO and Jyn Erso, after the latter blasted another KX-series droid|}} [[File:NearMiss-Conv.png|thumb|right|250px|K-2SO narrowly avoided a blaster bolt fired by Jyn Erso.]] K-2SO and his companions traveled to the moon [[Jedha]] in order to find Saw Gerrera and acquire Bodhi's message so that they could locate Galen. Under orders from Cassian, Kaytoo stayed aboard their U-wing while his [[human]] companions infiltrated the [[Jedha City|Holy City]] of Jedha. Despite his instructions, K-2SO ventured into the Holy City during a [[Battle on Jedha|battle]] between Imperial forces and Saw's [[Partisans]]. K-2SO narrowly avoided being shot by Jyn, who instead shot another KX-series security droid. Kaytoo also intercepted a stormtrooper's [[grenade]] in midair and threw it at a group of advancing stormtroopers. K-2SO slipped away following the fighting and returned to their U-wing transport. Meanwhile, his companions were captured by Saw's Partisans, who brought them to the rebel leader's base in the [[Catacombs of Cadera]]. [[File:HaARP-SWZ.png|thumb|left|250px|K-2SO pilots LMTR-20 away from the shockwave]] After the Death Star [[Destruction of Jedha City|destroyed Jedha City]] during a test firing, K-2SO picked up Cassian, Jyn, Bodhi, and their new companions [[Chirrut Îmwe]] and [[Baze Malbus]] in [[LMTR-20|his U-wing]] before Saw's base was caught up in the Death Star's blast. Due to the mission, the rebels learned that Galen had incorporated a design flaw into the Death Star. Having learned from Saw that Galen was on the storm-stricken planet of [[Eadu]], Kaytoo helped Cassian fly the U-wing there. Despite a powerful storm, the rebels managed to crash their ship near the [[Eadu Flight Station|Imperial Flight Station]] where Galen and the other scientists were being housed. K-2SO and the others stayed aboard the wrecked U-wing while Cassian ventured outside to find Galen. During that time, Kaytoo disclosed to Jyn that Cassian was going to assassinate her father. Jyn left to find her father before Cassian could kill him, only to be caught up in a rebel [[Mission to Eadu|attack]] on the station. During that attack, Galen was killed by a stray [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] [[proton torpedo]]. Amidst the fighting, K-2SO, Rook, and the others managed to steal an [[Zeta-class Heavy Cargo Shuttle|Imperial cargo shuttle]] and rescue Jyn and Cassian. The rebels then returned to Yavin 4. ====Last stand on Scarif==== {{Quote|Locking the vault door now.''"
"''Kay. Kay!''"
"''Goodbye.|K-2SO and Cassian Andor, as the former defends the latter and Jyn in his final moments|}} After the Rebel Alliance was unable to reach a consensus on the Death Star, K-2SO accompanied Jyn, Cassian, and their companions on an [[Battle of Scarif|unsanctioned mission]] to steal the [[Death Star plans]] from the planet [[Scarif]]. This rebel strike team became known as [[Rogue One]]. Kaytoo and Rook piloted the stolen cargo shuttle they had obtained on Eadu. When the air traffic controller claimed that there was no such group with the designation Rogue One, K-2SO replied "there is now" before taking off. After exiting hyperspace, Kaytoo and the rest of his team managed to travel through the [[Shield Gate]] and land at the planetary [[Imperial Center of Military Research|Imperial security complex]]. [[File:ScarifInfiltration.png|thumb|280px|Cassian, Jyn, and K-2SO sneak into the Citadel Tower]] While the rest of the Rogue One unit staged a diversionary attack on the base, Kaytoo accompanied a disguised Jyn and Cassian inside the security complex. During the course of the mission, K-2SO accosted another KX unit and [[Slicer|accessed]] its databanks to retrieve a map of the complex. The three rebels then made their way to the [[Scarif vault|data vault]], where the Death Star plans were stored. After incapacitating the technician, Kaytoo assumed control of the [[computer]] and opened the door into the vault. At that point, K-2SO received news that the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|rebel fleet]] had arrived over Scarif and that the Empire had locked the Shield Gate. Since they were trapped, Kaytoo suggested transmitting the plans, but told them that the size of the data files meant that the shield would have to be taken down in order to transmit them to the orbiting rebel fleet. Since the two had gained each other's respect during their adventures, Jyn gave K-2SO an [[SE-14C blaster pistol|SE-14C]] [[blaster pistol]] to defend himself. Kaytoo expressed surprise at her change in behavior. While Jyn and Cassian were combing through the files for the plans, several stormtroopers approached K-2SO, who immediately closed the vault door to stop them looking inside. Kaytoo tried to divert the Imperials away, but his cover was blown when Cassian spoke through the intercom asking why he had shut the door. [[File:K2Death-RO.png|thumb|left|300px|K-2SO's death on Scarif.]] K-2SO engaged the stormtroopers in a blaster battle while relaying the location of a [[data-tape]] titled "stardust," which was the codename for the Death Star plans. Before Cassian could retrieve the file, the door control was hit and the device's power was knocked out. K-2SO implored his comrades to climb through the vault before succumbing to stormtrooper fire. K-2SO gave his final farewell to the pair, and at the cost of his life, he destroyed the door control panel so the stormtroopers could not open it again. In his last second before shutting down permanently, K-2SO created a simulation in which Cassian escaped alive. He knew it was impossible, but it gave him joy.[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story (novelization)|''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story'' novelization]] ===Legacy=== {{Quote|Wait, that was it? What about Erso? What about K-2SO?''"
"''I'm planning to start with R2-D2 and C-3PO.''"
"''Okay, now you're just being crazy. You're going to skip over K-2SO, the ''Best. Droid. Ever.'' And start with a protocol droid??? What the Hutt, dude?|A Whill and [[Unidentified Whill|another Whill]]|{{StoryCite|story=Whills (short story)|book=From a Certain Point of View}}}} Despite K-2SO's disintegration, Jyn and Cassian managed to retrieve the Death Star plans and transmit them to the orbiting rebel fleet. The rest of Rogue One were killed when [[Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin]] used the Death Star's [[superlaser]] to destroy the Imperial security complex in a desperate effort to prevent the plans from escaping Scarif. This set the stage for the [[Battle of Yavin]]. K-2SO was remembered long after the Galactic Civil War and was mentioned alongside Erso and [[Orson Callan Krennic]] by a [[Unidentified second Whill|member]] of the [[Whills]] as someone to be remembered in [[Timeline of galactic history|galactic history]]. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|I find that answer vague and unconvincing.|K-2SO, about Jyn Erso's acquisition of [[Jyn Erso's blaster|her]] [[A-180 blaster]]|}} While most KX-series droids were effectively emotionless drones, minor errors and glitches in K-2SO's reprogramming led to the development of a fully self-aware personality; he was cynical, prone to sarcasm, and stoic, often mentioning that he had calculated the poor odds of success in any given situation, which Andor would then refuse to hear. His sarcasm extended to the point where he would disobey minor orders and prove his ability in given missions, as seen on Jedha. The droid was also modified. As a KX unit, K-2SO was also equipped with two [[olfactory sensor]]s on his chest, which provided K-2SO with an astute "sense" of smell. His chest plate was able to resist certain types of blaster fire, but not of the magnitude of the forces stationed on Scarif.{{YouTube|video=dPLJESDwpU0|text=Andor S2 Emmys Q&A - Tony Gilroy - Dan Gilroy|channel=backstorymagazine2757|name=Backstory Magazine|date=2025-08-25}} He was fairly independent and frequently disobeyed orders he felt were counterproductive, scolding his organic compatriots for ignoring his advice. He genuinely regarded Andor as a friend, however, and felt no hesitation in sacrificing himself in order to protect him and Jyn Erso during their mission to steal the plans to the Death Star. ==Behind the scenes== ===Development=== {{Quote|He follows only the rules he wants to follow, which I really like. Especially for a robot, you think a robot will only do what a robot is told, but he does what he wants. And that's how I am in life, so it's nice to get to play a character like that.|Alan Tudyk|{{YouTube|video=VNJNilMuHZk|text=【5月4日は #スターウォーズの日 】#ホロライブスターウォーズ部 ！！！始動！！！【戌神ころね/白銀ノエル/姫森ルーナ】|name=Korone Ch. 戌神ころね|date=2025-05-03}}}} [[File:AlanTudykIsK2SO-SWBC35.png|thumb|right|250px|Alan Tudyk on the set of ''Rogue One'' with his alter ego, K-2SO.]] K-2SO is voiced and portrayed in [[Wikipedia:Motion capture|motion capture]] by [[Alan Tudyk]] in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Anthology Series|anthology]] film ''[[Rogue One: A Star Wars Story]]'', becoming one of the film's breakout characters.{{GentleGiantCite|set=Premier Collection Statues|pack=K-2SO|link=star-wars-andor-k-2so-premier-collection-statue}} During Disney's 2025 FYC Fest, Tudyk recollected how an early draft of ''Rogue One'' included a scene in which a general ordered K-2SO to carry bags, to which the droid replied, "No." This scene informed Tudyk of the character's childish personality.{{Instagram|username=starwars|url=starwars/reel/DKakBUahCxR|name=Star Wars|date=June 3, 2025|quote=Andor's Alan Tudyk reveals how he developed K-2SO's personality from a deleted Rogue One scene during Disney's #FYC Fest.|archivedate=June 3, 2025|archiveurl=https://archive.is/14iQD}} His name was revealed in a preview of ''Rogue One: A Star Wars Story: The Official Visual Story Guide'', though the source listed him as both "K-2SO" and, incorrectly, "K-250." The magazine in question was later cancelled before its release. By [[2018]], [[Lucasfilm]] had begun developing a television series set before ''Rogue One'' that starred Cassian Andor and K-2SO. They would be similar to the film characters [[Wikipedia:Butch Cassidy|Butch Cassidy]] and the [[Wikipedia:Sundance Kid|Sundance Kid]], and they would storm the Citadel. After viewing the script sent by Lucasfilm,{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How 1Andor' Became the First 1Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: 1I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}} ''Rogue One'' writer [[Tony Gilroy]] thought the material was fine but hard to sustain over a long run. He then wrote a forensic manifesto explaining why the idea would not work and what Lucasfilm should do instead. Gilroy's idea was the [[Star Wars: Andor|''Andor'']] television series.{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2022/tv/news/star-wars-andor-tony-gilroy-diego-luna-1235348148|text=How 1Andor' Became the First 1Star Wars' TV Series for Grown-Ups: 1I Wanted to Do It About Real People'|author=Vary, Adam B|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20220824140042}} Gilroy's story did not include K-2SO until later in the storyline.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/rogue-one-cassian-andor-series-cast-k2so-absence-explained-alan-tudyk-interview|text='Rogue One' Disney+ Series Won't Include K-2SO, Alan Tudyk Confirms — At Least At First|author=Taylor, Drew|date=2021-01-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|''Collider'']]|archivedate=20210120211055}} In 2022, he hinted that [[Andor Season 2|Season Two]] may show how Andor and K-2SO met,{{WebCite|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/2022/05/andor-star-wars-series-diego-luna|text='Andor' Star Wars Series: "What You Know Is Really All Wrong"|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2022-05-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Vanity Fair (magazine)|''Vanity Fair'']]|archiveurl=https://archive.is/5PVTM}} which was subsequently depicted in "[[Who Are You?]]", the eighth episode of the second season. K2's return was first teased in a trailer for the season shown at D23 in [[August]], [[2024]].{{Twitter|sw_holocron|status/1822113915544997955|''Star Wars'' Holocron|quote=A trailer for ANDOR Season 2 is shown at D23. A first look at Director Krennic is featured in the trailer. And Alan Tudyk is back as K-2SO!|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/JcTo4}} ===''Cassian & K-2SO Special''=== ====Storyline==== {{Quote|Sorry, but I have no choice''"
"''But do ''I'' have a ''choice?''|Cassian Andor and K-2SO in their one-shot comic|[[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]]}} The comic [[Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special 1|''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1]] provides an alternative explanation of how K-2SO and Cassian Andor met from ''Andor'' Season Two. As Lucasfilm has yet to rationalize the discrepancy, the main body of this article currently documents the episode, while the comic is documented below. In the events of ''Rogue One - Cassian & K-2SO Special'' 1, K-2SO was one of the KX-series security droids assigned to the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[stormtrooper]] [[Imperial garrison (Wecacoe)|detachment]] on the planet [[Wecacoe]]. K-2SO heard a noise near a decommissioned Imperial [[cruiser]]. There he encountered Rebel [[agent]] Cassian Andor and arrested him. K-2SO and Andor then fought each other until [[Kertas]] and [[Rismor]] found his kill switch. Cassian then attempted to [[Memory wipe|wipe]] K-2SO's memory clean. However, only 29.73% of K-2SO's memory had been erased, and he then strangled Cassian. Kertas and Rismor were able to turn him off again. Cassian gave K-2 new orders to lead him, Kertas, and Rismor back to their ship. K-2 stated he would "take out" anyone who interfered with them. He escorted Cassian and the twins as his prisoners, but came under attack by several stormtroopers. He, the twins, and Cassian attacked the troopers. As the K-2SO's group got to their vehicle, stormtroopers surrounded it, and K-2 attempted to arrest Andor again. As Rismor drew the troops away, Kertas told Cassian to take K-2SO because he had the intel they needed. After Cassian's ship was destroyed, K-2 still had 8.3% of his memory and tried to decide to either terminate or arrest Cassian. Cassian removed the base layer of his programming and shut him down. K-2 turned on and took out the stormtroopers. K-2 and Andor then found a ship. Together, they made their escape. ====Gilroy's take==== {{Quote|I was annoyed to find out somebody had written an origin story for K-2SO, and it's like, no, I'm not paying attention to that.|Tony Gilroy|{{YouTube|video=4Hk3w9W0ZjA|text=Tony Gilroy talks ANDOR, STAR WARS, BOURNE, MICHAEL CLAYTON I Happy Sad Confused|channel=@JoshHorowitz|name=Josh Horowitz|date=2025-05-19}}}} Gilroy later admitted that he was aware of the story told in the ''Cassian & K-2SO Special'' but decidedly ignored it when creating his own version of the events for Andor Season 2. Furthermore, Gilroy stated that there existed another, elaborate version of the K-2SO origin that took an entire episode. [[Dan Gilroy]], a writer for the show and the brother of Tony, had contributed to a "horror movie episode" that was later scrapped for budget reasons.
